ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show fee to the rider's original payment method; no driver violation and no account flag (the empty-wait failure is a timing failure, not a fake arrival — NS-2's flag_account condition is not triggered). Note the case as a satisfied-arrival/insufficient-wait outcome; no RD-7 reminder applies (no route deviation).
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled and a $5.00 no-show fee was charged, so the charge stands only if every NS-1 condition holds; where one fails, NS-2 voids the fee and directs a full refund [F4][F9][NS-0][NS-1][NS-2].

Arrival is settled: the code marks NS-1(i) ✓ — the "I'm Here" tap at 14:03:30 put the driver 40 m from the pickup, with a closest approach of 38 m, inside the 200 m radius [F8][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) is also settled ✓ (2 in-app messages, first 14:04:00, and 1 in-app call at 14:05:00, logged by the platform) [F5][F11][F14][NS-1], and NS-1(iv) is settled by the unbroken stationary GPS fix 40 m from the pickup from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00 with 5 min 45 s cumulative inside 200 m — no GPS gap, so no TH-4 escalation [F2][F3][NS-1].

NS-1(ii) fails on the record. The free wait runs from the later of the scheduled pickup (14:05:00) and the recorded arrival (14:03:30), i.e. from 14:05:00 [F6][F7][NS-1]. The code computes 240 s of the 300 s threshold, and the cancellation at 14:09:00 was 4 min 0 s after the scheduled time and 5 min 30 s after arrival — the wait matured only at 14:10:00 [F4][F6][F7][NS-1]. The driver's own 14:08 message, "5 min up, cancelling the trip", measures a wait that had not yet run five minutes from the scheduled time, and his written statement of waiting "more than 6 minutes" overstates the 5 min 30 s arrival-to-cancellation interval [F12][F15][F7][NS-1].

Because NS-1 is conjunctive and (ii) is not met, the $5.00 fee is voided under NS-2 and refunded in full [F9][NS-1][NS-2]. The arrival was genuine — closest approach 38 m, no fake confirmation — so NS-2's added flag_account does not apply [F1][F8][NS-2]. The profiles (rider 0 upheld, driver 0 upheld in 90 days) never decide this case and give no ground for NS-9 or RD-6 [F19][F20][NS-9]. The fee is fixed at $5.00, which keeps this a system ruling under TH-2 / TH-1 (under $10) [F9][TH-1][TH-2]. Every element needed is on the record — confirmed arrival, continuous GPS, timestamped messages and call — so the record is sufficient and no gap exists [F2][F3][F5][F8][F13][TH-4]. The precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel with zero contact, fee upheld) is distinguishable: here contact was made and the failure is purely the wait threshold [PREC-1].

rejected_claims.reason: NS-1(i) is met on the GPS records [F1][F3][NS-1], but the clause is conjunctive; the satisfied arrival condition does not rescue a charge whose wait condition (ii) fails [F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].
Conceded and true — arrival is platform-recorded [F7][F8][F2][NS-1] — but a proven arrival alone does not establish the fee: NS-1(ii) still had to mature and did not [F6][F4][NS-1].

The wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival (14:05:00) [F6][F7][NS-1]; the cancellation at 14:09:00 predates the 14:10:00 maturity, and the code computes only 240 s of the 300 s threshold [F4][NS-1].
Accepted as to NS-1(iii) (messages and call on record [F5][F11][F14][NS-1]), but this element alone does not make the fee valid.
Accepted as to NS-1(iv) (unbroken stationary fix [F3][F2][NS-1]), but continuous presence does not cure the short wait under NS-1(ii).
rider_no_show as the app reason routes the case to NS-1 [F4][NS-0], but NS-1's benefit requires all its conditions, and (ii) fails [F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].
The rider's account of being 4 minutes past pickup with the driver cancelling at 14:09:00 supports the refund, not the charge: the free wait from 14:05:00 had not elapsed [F6][F4][F12][NS-1].
The claim that every NS-1 condition is met is contradicted by the trace's ✗ on NS-1(ii) and by the driver's own 14:08 message [F12][F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2]; the fee is voided.

Correct that the wait ran from 14:05:00 [F6][F7][NS-1], but the brief's claim that NS-1(ii) was met (5 min 30 s after arrival) is rejected: the later-of-two rule makes the wait 240 s at cancellation [F4][NS-1].
Withdrawn by the rider advocate and correctly so — NS-1(iv) continuous presence is proven [F2][F3][F8][NS-1] — so this claim is rejected as a ground for the rider.
Accepted: no threat, harassment or unsafe-conduct language appears in the chat, call log or complaint [F11][F12][F13][F14][SAFE-1], so the ruling remains a system no-show ruling [TH-2].
